title: PostgreSQL Extension Architecture & pg_trgm
description: Explore the extension ecosystem, understand CREATE EXTENSION mechanics, and build fuzzy search with pg_trgm.

data.text: PostgreSQL's hallmark feature is its extension system. Extensions can register custom C code, new index types, operators, and background worker daemons directly into the database engine without modifying PostgreSQL core.

data.title: Fuzzy String Similarity with pg_trgm
data.content: Finding matching usernames even with typos.

data.text: `CREATE EXTENSION` loads a packaged module into a database; the module's files must already be installed on the server by the operating system package manager or built from source. Extensions are versioned, and `ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE` moves an installed extension to a newer version.

data.title: Install, list, and upgrade extensions
data.content: `pg_available_extensions` shows what the server can install; `pg_extension` shows what each database has already installed.

data.title: Interview angle: extensions are a strength and a portability risk
data.text: One of PostgreSQL's best answers to 'how do I add this feature?' is 'there is an extension'. But extensions are C code that runs inside the server process with full access to your data, so they must be versioned and reviewed like any dependency. Some are not available on managed services, and some break across major upgrades until the package is rebuilt. Mentioning availability, upgrade path, and trust level is what distinguishes a thoughtful answer.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `CREATE EXTENSION` registers shared libraries into PostgreSQL.
`pg_trgm` breaks strings into 3-character trigrams to support fuzzy search and indexed `LIKE '%abc%'` queries.
Extensions allow PostgreSQL to replace specialized search, vector, and time-series databases.
